input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right exercisable by TrueLink against Client. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books" and "monitor" return nothing, and the sections where such rights are usually tucked away are clean: § 5–6 (Compensation/Documentation) runs in our favour, giving Client the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges rather than giving TrueLink reconciliation audit rights; § 8 (Client covenants) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties with no verification right; § 10 (Confidentiality) contains no inspection mechanic. The only related items are TrueLink's right under § 8(f) to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted Interface to prevent spamming/illegal use, and Client's Y2K-related obligation in § 9 to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's own repairs at TrueLink's cost — neither is a usage audit nor grants access to Client systems or records. With no audit right binding us, there is no exposure on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, so the playbook position is satisfied and no redline is needed.
